label: r4c1
name: r2c2 with 32 minibatches
hypothesis: Same as r2c2, with 32 minibatches instead of 16 (64 samples each). This doubles the gradient steps per update (about 7.6k in total) while keeping the samples and the 79 updates. r3c1 to r2c2 suggests that more gradient steps help. Refuted if 2-seed dev success is at or below 0.90, or a seed collapses.
last_analysis: Flipping each placement score map in x so it lines up with the action indices was the decisive change. Every trial without it collapsed to choosing DONE (0.0); with it the same start net reached 0.67 under the default recipe. More policy updates then raised this to 0.90 in r2c2, which used 128 envs, 3 epochs and 16 minibatches, giving 79 updates and about 3.8k gradient steps. The variants of r2c2 all did worse. Cutting to 2 epochs and 8 minibatches (r3c1) gave 0.07 with only about 1.8k gradient steps. Adding a global broadcast gave 0.86/0.40. Raising gamma to 0.99 gave 0.95 on one seed and 0.0 on the other. Results vary hugely between seeds, and one failure mode is a seed that never learns. The pattern so far is that more optimiser updates and gradient steps help. When the trained net does work, its failures are rare wrong cells (0.25 extra cells per episode), which points to how precisely the head judges each footprint. This round tests more gradient steps, more updates, and a deeper footprint head.
